short: A Sunday morning raid on Hawaii that brought the United States into the war.
full:
Six Japanese carriers approached Hawaii undetected and launched 353 aircraft in two waves from 7.48am on 7 December 1941. Torpedoes fitted with wooden fins to run in shallow water struck battleship row; Arizona blew up when a bomb reached her forward magazine, killing 1,177 men. Eight battleships were sunk or damaged, 188 aircraft destroyed and 2,403 Americans killed. Coordinated attacks fell the same day on the Philippines, Malaya, Hong Kong and Guam.

The raid was a tactical success and a strategic disaster. The American carriers were at sea and survived, and the dockyards, submarine base and fuel storage were left untouched, so all but two of the sunk battleships were eventually raised and returned to service. Isolationist opinion in the United States collapsed overnight and Congress declared war the next day with a single dissenting vote. Germany declared war on the United States on 11 December, joining the European and Pacific conflicts into a single global war.
